title: Naturality of the Jacobi-Zariski connecting map for a quotient
statement: Let $R\to S\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, $I\subseteq B$ an ideal and $C=B/I$, an $S$-algebra and an $R$-algebra through $B$. For a ring map $X\to Y$ let $H_1(L_{Y/X})$ be the first homology of the naive cotangent complex of the canonical presentation $X[Y]\to Y$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; let $\Omega$, $\mathrm d$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let (a) $\iota:H_1(L_{C/S})\to H_1(L_{C/B})$ be the map induced by the morphism of presentations $S[C]\to B[C]$ (coefficients through $S\to B$, $[c]\mapsto[c]$) over the square $S\to B$, $\mathrm{id}_C$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]; (b) $\theta:H_1(L_{C/B})\xrightarrow{\sim}I/I^2$ the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1] for the surjection $B\to C$; (c) $\partial_S:H_1(L_{C/S})\to C\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}$ the connecting map of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $R\to S\to C$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence]; (d) $c:C\otimes_S\Omega_{S/R}\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R}$, $x\otimes\mathrm ds\mapsto x\otimes\mathrm d(s\cdot1_B)$, and $\delta:I/I^2\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R}$, $f\bmod I^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm df$. Then $$\delta\circ\theta\circ\iota=c\circ\partial_S .$$ In particular (case $S=B$, where $\iota$ and $c$ are identities) $\delta\circ\theta=\partial_B$: under $\theta$ the connecting map of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $R\to B\to C$ is $\delta$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Section Tag 07E4 (section-geometrically-regular, line 8678): 'The Jacobi-Zariski sequence is a canonical exact sequence H_1(L_{K/k}) -> m/m^2 -> Omega_{A/k} (x)_A K -> Omega_{K/k} -> 0 because H_1(L_{K/A}) = m/m^2'; and the commutative diagram in the proof of Proposition 07E5, equivalence of (3) and (4) (line 8752); the maps of Algebra Lemma Tag 00S2 (line 35412), whose proof says 'The precise definition of the maps is omitted'.
